info.title: statusd.py: what the web app and other machines' fleets rely on
info.description: The HTTP boundary between statusd.py and its clients: the React app at /app/ (served by this or another configured machine; cross-origin reads and posts are allowed only for the origins in statusd.CORS_ORIGINS) and, for the two peer endpoints, other machines' fleet servers at other versions (runnerlib/backends.py). Decision: web/context/decisions/0002-statusd-http-contract.md. Checked by tests/test_web_contract.py with web/scripts/contract_check.py. Schemas use only the JSON Schema keywords that validator enforces (it refuses any other). Schemas describe what statusd SENDS; a reader must still ignore fields it does not know. x-tier: peer = read across machines and versions, additive changes only; app = read only by the app served from the same checkout. x-ts names the TypeScript interface in web/src/model/payload.ts that reads the schema; x-ts-client-only lists fields that interface adds itself after the fetch.

get.summary: Cheap, polled: changes whenever anything the fleet shows for this machine changed.
Everything the fleet renders for this machine (statusd.fleet_payload).
What the New work dialog needs beside /api/fleet: the home directory and the skill picker's library.
Real directories on this machine completing q, as a shell would. Directory names only.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: a path prefix; ~ expands; at most 400 characters are read

get.summary: Spend: totals and the same spend cut by node, project and task (runnerlib/costs.summarize). The costs screen reads it.

The fleet stream (Server-Sent Events). It carries no data to draw: on hello and change the client re-fetches /api/fleet. Comment lines (': ping') keep it open. The server closes on error; a client falls back to polling /api/fleet.

post.summary: Launch work. Empty text, a missing submitter or a refused task is answered with a notice, not an HTTP error.
Change one item's done, hidden or tag marks (items.json). A refused change is a 'Refused: ...' notice.
Move, replace, end, archive or attach a conversation. Lands on /page/<key>, or on / for an archive with back=home that was not refused. A refused repair is a 'Refused: ...' notice.
Create a project. Lands on /project/<id>, or on / when refused. (/projects/<id>/tasks and /projects/<id>/archive join this contract with the project screen.)

get.summary: The machines the app can switch between: this one first (url "" = where the app was loaded from), then each configured [[backends]] entry, which the app reads and posts to directly.
The library screen's data: everything installed that a launch can pick (library.scan), and the project folders scanned.
The costs screen's data: costs.summarize over every finished turn; the same body as /costs.json.
The runs screen's data for one view: its rows (at most `limit`), how many there are, and every project and node a filter can pick.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description: latest | open | turns | failed; anything else is latest

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: task, project or page title contains (hyphens read as spaces)

get.summary: The session-tree screen's data: every session that launched or was launched, by task (session_tree.load).

The project page's data: the project, its group and members, its open conversations with what the fleet reads about them, what finished and is starting, its context store, what a task launched here is told, and the library its launcher offers. The Python /project/<id> renders from the same function.

The manage page's data for any round of a conversation: the conversation, the projects it can move to, the conversations that can replace it, and who owns the page. The Python /page/<key> renders from the same function.

Landing.description: Asked with Accept: application/json: where the post landed and what happened, instead of the 303.

Landed.description: A plain browser post: Location is <path>?notice=<what happened>, so a refresh does not re-post.

CrossOrigin.description: cross-origin post (an Origin that is not this host). Body is text, not part of the contract.

UnknownAction.description: unknown action path. Body is text, not part of the contract.

TooLarge.description: body too large. Body is text, not part of the contract.

instance.description: this server process's id; same instance = this machine

review_events.description: whether this machine's page server is streaming its events to us

graph.description: [link records, holders, pages by key]. Exactly three: older readers unpack it.

Snapshot.description: The runner's status.json, passed through (open: the daemon owns it).

Surface.description: A review page the runner registered (status.json surfaces). Open: the daemon owns it.

role.description: "orchestrator" for a terminal session that runs others

SessionStatus.description: A page's live state from the page server (open: review-surface owns it).

type.description: supersedes | continues | child-of today; a reader skips a type it does not know

launcher.description: the session that launched this one, when this machine does not know it as a task

RecentRow.description: A recently finished task (recent.rows). The app does not read it yet.

d.description: the start of its description, at most 120 characters

notice.description: what happened, in words for the driver

location.description: <path>?notice=..., the page a browser post would land on

text.description: required in practice: empty text is a notice

parent.description: the item's task id this work joins

target.description: replace: the page that replaces key

back.description: home: an archive stays on the fleet

dir1.description: the directory launched work runs in

page.description: the task's newest page's session record (recent.pages_by_task; open: the page server writes it); the app reads path, key and title

TurnRecord.description: a cost-log turn record, newest first (open: the runner writes it)

ClosedPage.description: a page of the project that has ended (statusd.closed_pages; open: built from the page server's records)

row.description: the conversation's head row as conversations.conversation_of returns it (a Surface with earlier, page_title and ended; open)
